assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines the physiology of proglucagon-derived GLP-1 as an incretin and its translation into therapies that have changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Originality of the basic discovery, a clear change in the field, and very large, still-growing clinical impact make this a leading candidate.
assessment.attribution: Basic discovery credit is plausibly carried by Holst (incretin physiology, bioactive GLP-1(7-36) in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and GLP-2) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide); Habener is not on the supplied list. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen led industrial development of the long-acting agonists but a three-person cap forces a choice between discovery and drug development.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs and large outcome trials make the interpretation stable. Timing is highly favorable given the current scale of impact.
uncertainties: Allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and the unlisted early contributors is contested and I cannot verify the details independently.
Whether the committee prefers recognizing the basic physiology or the drug-development component is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of an intracellular signaling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with conserved IRE1/ATF6/PERK arms, is a fundamental cell-biological mechanism with broad relevance to secretory physiology, neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Mori (cis-element and transcriptional response in mammals and yeast) and Walter (IRE1 as sensor, Hac1 splicing mechanism) form a natural pair; the supplied credit supports a clean two-person prize. Other contributors, for example in PERK and ATF6 biology, are not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is deeply confirmed across organisms over thirty years and the textbook status is secure. Recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether further contributors beyond the two named would be considered necessary by the committee is uncertain.
The direct medical consequences are more indirect than for therapeutic candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated channelrhodopsins turned into a general tool for causal control of genetically defined cells have transformed neuroscience and are used in cardiac, retinal and other work, including early clinical vision restoration. Originality is high and the methodological impact is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Six credited names exceed the three-person limit. Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin function; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal use; Bamberg contributed to the channel work and Miesenboeck to earlier genetically encoded light control. The cut-off is difficult and I choose the channel discovery plus the principal neuronal implementation.
assessment.maturity: Widely validated over about twenty years. Therapeutic translation is early, but the tool value is firmly established, so recognition would not be premature.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Boyden, Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg and Miesenboeck is genuinely disputed and I cannot resolve it from the supplied text.
Whether a methods-oriented discovery fits the category's emphasis on physiology or medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and elucidation of mTOR complexes as the central regulator of growth and nutrient sensing is a major conceptual advance with relevance to cancer, metabolism, immunity, ageing and transplantation drugs.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and established its role in growth control; Sabatini (and colleagues) identified mammalian mTOR and the core complex architecture and nutrient-sensing arms. Schreiber contributed the chemical biology of rapamycin/FKBP12 and is a plausible third. Credit among mTOR identification groups is intertwined.
assessment.maturity: Very extensively confirmed, with clinical use of rapalogs and a vast literature; timing is mature.
uncertainties: Recipient selection among Hall, Sabatini, Schreiber and other mTOR-purification groups is uncertain, including the early mammalian mTOR identification credit.
Any non-scientific considerations about individuals fall outside what I can evaluate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines preventing HPV infection are a landmark in cancer prevention, with population-level evidence of reduced cervical precancer and cancer. Importance and lasting impact are very high, although the zur Hausen prize already recognized the HPV-cancer link.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs at NCI and Frazer (with the late Jian Zhou) developed the Queensland VLP technology; Zhou's death complicates the configuration. Lowy, Schiller and Frazer are the supplied credit set; priority interplay between groups is something I cannot judge fully.
assessment.maturity: Registration trials and real-world surveillance data in multiple countries confirm effect; the cancer-incidence signal is increasingly direct, so timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims among VLP groups and Zhou's posthumous role are unresolved.
Vaccine development may be viewed as downstream of an already-awarded discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS-generated cGAMP and STING-dependent signaling is a new core pathway of innate immunity, implicated in infection, autoimmunity, senescence and cancer immunotherapy. Originality and breadth are high.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger; Barber identified STING. Hiroki Ishikawa is credited with early STING work, and Sun and Wu were in Chen's group; a two-person configuration is the cleanest, but ordering of credit between STING discovery groups is debated.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistically well confirmed, but therapeutic validation (STING agonists, inhibitors) is still maturing, so some prematurity risk remains.
uncertainties: Credit for STING identification is shared with other groups and I cannot verify precise priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing, culminating in nusinersen, converted a lethal pediatric disease into a treatable one and established a template for splice-modulating oligonucleotide therapy.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and identified the ISS-N1 target-based design strategy; Bennett led antisense chemistry and clinical development. This is a coherent two-person translational pairing, though contributions by others, for example the original SMN gene discovery and other splicing groups, are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical follow-up showing durable benefit; the concept is confirmed, while the broader impact on other diseases continues to develop.
uncertainties: The prize could be seen as mainly a therapeutic achievement and the role of other SMN groups is not reflected in the supplied credit.
Long-term outcome data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis, with proof-of-concept in patients, opened anti-cytokine therapy and altered outcomes for many chronic inflammatory diseases. The impact is large and the concept is clear.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly drove the mechanistic rationale and the clinical proof-of-concept, which supports a fair two-person prize. Others who developed the antibodies and TNF biology itself (for example Cerami, Old, Vilcek) are outside the supplied credit, which complicates a clean attribution.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of clinical experience and multiple drug classes confirm efficacy; timing is mature, perhaps overdue if the committee values it.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as underweighting the TNF biology and antibody engineering contributors.
Recognition of a therapeutic concept may be judged against more fundamental discoveries.
